touch_updater: rebind_driver() now supports recovering non-enumerated devices Previously rebind_driver() would determine the /sys driver path based on the driver/ symlink in the device directory. However if the device did not enumerate on boot because its firmware is corrupt, there will be no driver/ symlink. Now it's possible to specify a driver path. BUG=b:132830741 TEST=Tested both normal update and firmware corruption recovery with etphidiap updater. No behavior changes, as expected (new arg not yet specified). Then tested again with CL:1772379, and with that the driver bind succeeds after corruption recovery reflash, and the touch device is immediately usable on that same boot. Change-Id: I3a4e080e8c86095b8fb6c14531d9f37d3a164c5d Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1772378 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean O'Brien <seobrien@chromium.org>

touch_updater: etphidiap updater now binds driver after corrupted FW recovery. Previously this updater script was able to reflash to recover from correupted firmware, but the common rebind_driver() function was not able to handle binding the driver in that scenario, so the touch device would only become functional again after an extra reboot. Now this takes advantage of a new rebind_driver() option to specify the driver path, in order to recover devices that did not enumerate on startup. BUG=b:132830741 TEST=Tested both normal update and firmware corruption recovery with etphidiap updater. The normal case continues to work, including the rebind. The corruption recovery case now successfully binds after reflash, and the touch device is immediately usable on that same boot. Cq-Depend: chromium:1772378 Change-Id: I0678e548bee7050e4d7e3a05a71f1c63393b278d Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1772379 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean O'Brien <seobrien@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ipv6: set rt6i_protocol properly in the route when it is installed After commit c2ed1880fd61 ("net: ipv6: check route protocol when deleting routes"), ipv6 route checks rt protocol when trying to remove a rt entry. It introduced a side effect causing 'ip -6 route flush cache' not to work well. When flushing caches with iproute, all route caches get dumped from kernel then removed one by one by sending DELROUTE requests to kernel for each cache. The thing is iproute sends the request with the cache whose proto is set with RTPROT_REDIRECT by rt6_fill_node() when kernel dumps it. But in kernel the rt_cache protocol is still 0, which causes the cache not to be matched and removed. So the real reason is rt6i_protocol in the route is not set when it is allocated. As David Ahern's suggestion, this patch is to set rt6i_protocol properly in the route when it is installed and remove the codes setting rtm_protocol according to rt6i_flags in rt6_fill_node. This is also an improvement to keep rt6i_protocol consistent with rtm_protocol.
